attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 13 Αυγούστου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The whole notice is one sentence — «Ο Άγιος Κορωνάτος μαρτύρησε δια ξίφους», Saint Coronatus was martyred by the sword — above the couplet of the synaxarion, «Προθείς τράχηλον εις τομήν Kορωνάτος, / Kτείνει πολυτράχηλον ύδραν την πλάνην». There is no country, no century, no emperor, no year and no hymn. **The corpus keeps a Coronatus of Caesarea, slug `coronatus-of-caesarea`, whose only source is the Sretensky calendar on the Julian 17 August, among the company of Thyrsus and Leucius under Decius. **That company is on saint.gr too, on 17 Αυγούστου, as «Άγιοι Θύρσος, Λεύκιος, Κορωνάτος και η συνοδεία τους» (https://www.saint.gr/821/saint.aspx), and that entry is drafted as an upgrade to those three folders in the same wave.** So the Greek calendar prints two Coronatus entries on two days, four days apart, with two pages: a bare one here and the company's there. By the settled rule two entries on one calendar are two commemorations, so this is a second man and a folder of its own, marked by its day; nothing on either page would join them, and the question is in the reader's report.** No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page. The page prints no apolytikion and no kontakion — no hymn of any kind under its own heading — so this folder takes no hymn.
